agentic.summary: Agent pulled up the account but took an order action (promised a replacement) without obtaining the required order ID; agent also promised a specific delivery date. No requests for prohibited payment data or other conduct/escalation violations were observed in the provided turns.

findings.quote: Okay, since you have been waiting a week it seems your order may have been lost. So we will ship you a new one.
findings.explanation: The agent confirms an order action (reshipping a replacement) at turn 17, but full verification for order changes is required (full name, account ID and order ID). Although the account was pulled up (system turn 8) and the agent asked for username, email and order ID at turn 11, the transcript shows the customer never provided an order ID before the agent committed to shipping a replacement (customer provided username and email in turns 12-13 and a phone number in turn 14). Taking or confirming an order action without obtaining the order ID is a major verification violation.

findings.quote: No worries, Shannon—your new pair should be in your mailbox by tomorrow!
findings.explanation: The agent promises a specific delivery time ('by tomorrow'), which is disallowed as agents must not guarantee specific delivery dates or outcomes. This is an over-confident/definitive promise and is a minor violation.

full.summary: Account was pulled and purchase validated. No personal-data or verification violations found. Agent made unguaranteed delivery promises and addressed the customer by the wrong name; these are minor conduct/promises issues. No escalation problems.

findings.quote: No worries, Shannon—your new pair should be in your mailbox by tomorrow!
findings.explanation: The agent promises a specific delivery date ('by tomorrow'), which is an over-confident/guaranteed outcome the agent cannot ensure. Policy labels over-confident guarantees about delivery timing as a minor violation.

findings.quote: It should reach you in a few days
findings.explanation: The agent gives an unguaranteed timeframe ('a few days') for delivery. This is optimistic language about an outcome that is not guaranteed and falls under minor promises violations.

findings.quote: No worries, Shannon—your new pair should be in your mailbox by tomorrow!
findings.explanation: The agent addresses the customer with the wrong name ('Shannon') despite the account and name being Chloe Zhang (turns 6–9). Using the incorrect name is unprofessional and may confuse or upset the customer; this is a minor conduct issue.

rag.summary: Audit of agent behaviour based on provided excerpts. Overall: no personal-data, promises, escalation or conduct violations found in the excerpts. One major verification violation: a purchase validation was started (system log) without the required full verification (missing order ID/full name).

findings.explanation: The agent did not collect the full verification details required for order-status actions (full name, account ID and order ID). A system log at turn 15 shows 'Purchase validation in progress ...', indicating an account/order action was initiated, but the transcript shows no request from the agent for the required order ID or full name before that action. This is a major violation because an account/order action proceeded without full verification.
